changes.summary: Every page now wears one icon wherever it's linked: the menu, search, page cards, draft and Front Office tabs and homepage tiles all match.

Tip Schefter now sits first in the header's icon row, one tap from any page.
On a phone, the homepage shows the Schefter Report right under the hero, then your team and the standings. The Owners' Poll card is gone; the weekly pop-up stays.
The Broadcast has a home in MFL Live at /live/broadcast, with a live preview, one-tap full screen and TV pairing by QR code.
changes.headline: Put your Sunday on the TV
changes.lede: The Broadcast now lives in MFL Live. Watch every league's scores in a live preview, go full screen in one tap, or pair a TV by scanning a QR code with your phone.
changes.imageAlt: The MFL Live Broadcast page, with the live scoreboard playing inside a TV frame beside the Go full screen button.

changes.summary: The Broadcast fits your phone or tablet now: matchup cards that fit a sideways phone, plays as slide-in banners, and the screen stays awake.
On a phone or tablet, tap a Broadcast matchup to see both starting lineups, then tap a player for points and projection.
On a sideways phone, swipe through Broadcast matchups a screen at a time, and see which of your players are on the field right now.
Use your phone as a remote for a paired TV on the Broadcast: focus one league, flip the player strip, or mute it from the couch.
Every page on the site now speaks Primetime: headings in italic broadcast caps, and section titles marked by a short slanted underline instead of the old editorial stripe.
Cards across the site drop their outlines and float on a soft shadow instead, in light and dark.
Rosters and Live Scoring put the teams first: big crests and broadcast-style names, with card outlines gone in dark mode too.
Search from any page: the magnifying glass in the header now opens a search box right where you are, finding pages and players as you type.

Halloween comes to TheLeague: for two NFL weeks through Nov 2, the site goes black, white and orange, with spooky headlines and every team wearing its black-and-white mark.
Halloween comes to the AFL: for two NFL weeks through Nov 2, the site goes black, white and orange, with spooky headlines and every team wearing its black-and-white mark.
On the Rosters page, the team switcher now opens the selected team's conference and scrolls to its crest, so you can always see which team you're on, phone included.
Throwback Week moves to Week 11 (Nov 19-23), so it no longer lands in the middle of Halloween week. Your era pick carries over.
For Halloween, Live Scoring opens on a haunted house under a full moon, with the week's Monster of the Week and Scariest Game called out up top.
The Brand Book now holds every file: league, conference and division pages, a retired-clubs archive, the Halloween marks, and a search that finds any file by name.
